aliases: topos is Set-like: limits, colimits, cartesian closed, epi-mono factorization, subobject classifier
finitely complete and cocomplete cartesian closed category with Ω

evidence.intree_statement: Class ElementaryTopos (C : Category) := { topos_terminal : @Terminal C; topos_cartesian : @Cartesian C; topos_pullbacks : @HasPullbacks C; topos_closed : @Closed C topos_cartesian; topos_classifier : @SubobjectClassifier C topos_terminal }.
Theorem classifier_classifies (x : C) : @Isomorphism Sets {| carrier := SubObj x |} {| carrier := x ~> Ω |}.

Definition FinSet_Topos : ElementaryTopos FinSet := {| topos_terminal := FinSet_Terminal; topos_cartesian := FinSet_Cartesian; topos_pullbacks := FinSet_Pullbacks; topos_closed := FinSet_Closed; topos_classifier := FinSet_Classifier |}.

statement_record.book: Any topos E enjoys five Set-like properties, asserted without proof: (i) it has all limits, (ii) it has all colimits, (iii) it is cartesian closed, (iv) every morphism has an epi-mono factorization, (v) it has a subobject classifier true : 1 → Ω. Since Set is a topos, all five hold for Set.
statement_record.intree: Class ElementaryTopos (C : Category) := { topos_terminal : @Terminal C; topos_cartesian : @Cartesian C; topos_pullbacks : @HasPullbacks C; topos_closed : @Closed C topos_cartesian; topos_classifier : @SubobjectClassifier C topos_terminal }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: three of the five clauses are in force, and two are absent. (iii) cartesian closure and (v) the subobject classifier are carried as class fields (with the classification theorem classifier_classifies : SubObj x ≅ (x ~> Ω) and a computable witness FinSet_Topos), so they are present but as AXIOMS of the in-tree class rather than as derived properties — which matches the standard elementary-topos definition and is not a defect. (i) 'all limits' is only partly in force: finite-limit data is carried explicitly as terminal object + binary products + pullbacks, and the file header discloses that the reduction of pullbacks to products and equalizers is deliberately not formalized, so there is no finite-completeness (let alone Complete) theorem for a topos, and no equalizer field. (ii) all colimits and (iv) epi-mono factorization in a topos have NO in-tree counterpart at all: ElementaryTopos has no cocartesian/initial/colimit field, there is no `Complete`/`Cocomplete` instance for any topos, and the only OFS instances are Regular_OFS (regular categories) and Abelian_OFS (abelian categories), neither derived from ElementaryTopos.

gap: Two of the five asserted properties are missing for a topos: (a) COLIMITS — ElementaryTopos carries no initial object, coproducts or colimits, and there is no theorem that an elementary topos is (finitely) cocomplete; (b) EPI-MONO FACTORIZATION in a topos — there is no instance `OFS EpiClass MonoClass` derived from ElementaryTopos, nor a `Regular C` instance derived from it (`Structure/Regular.v` has no instances at all in-tree). Additionally (c) the LIMITS clause is only partly in force: the class stipulates terminal + binary products + pullbacks and the header states that no reduction to general finite limits is formalized, so 'has all limits' is not available as a theorem. Clauses (iii) and (v) are fully in force.

verifier.notes: Blind pass reached PARTIAL independently and by the same route. Confirmed at the cited locations: Structure/Topos.v:112 Class ElementaryTopos has exactly the five fields quoted (terminal, cartesian, pullbacks, closed, classifier) — no initial/cocartesian/colimit and no factorization field; Structure/SubobjectClassifier.v:187 classifier_classifies is verbatim; Instance/FinSet/Topos.v:38 FinSet_Topos is verbatim. Independent negative checks I ran: `rg ElementaryTopos` over the whole tree returns exactly 7 hits (Structure/Topos.v x3, Construction/Slice.v:114 prose, Instance/FinSet/Topos.v:38) — nothing derives limits, colimits or a factorization FROM ElementaryTopos; Structure/Complete.v:115/119 define Complete/Cocomplete but no instance exists for any topos (`rg Sets_Complete|Cocomplete Sets` = 0 hits); the only OFS instances in the tree are Structure/Abelian.v:441 (Abelian_OFS) and Structure/Regular/Factorization.v:282 (Regular_OFS), and `rg` for a `Regular C` INSTANCE returns none at all (only Structure/Regular.v:66 Class Regular and Structure/Regular/Factorization.v:125 `Context (R : Regular C)`), so the classifier's claim is exact. evidence.intree_statement: Lemma pullback_paste (HQ : IsPullback h m Q q1 q2) (HP : IsPullback k q1 P p1 p2) : IsPullback (h ∘ k) m P p1 (q2 ∘ p2).

Record IsPullback {C} {x y z : C} (f : x ~> z) (g : y ~> z) (P : C) (p1 : P ~> x) (p2 : P ~> y) := { is_pullback_commutes : f ∘ p1 ≈ g ∘ p2; is_pullback_ump : ∀ Q (q1 : Q ~> x) (q2 : Q ~> y), f ∘ q1 ≈ g ∘ q2 → ∃! u : Q ~> P, p1 ∘ u ≈ q1 ∧ p2 ∘ u ≈ q2 }.

statement_record.book: Given a commutative diagram of two adjacent squares over composable rows, with the right-hand square a pullback: the left-hand square is a pullback if and only if the outer rectangle is a pullback.
statement_record.intree: pullback_paste : IsPullback h m Q q1 q2 → IsPullback k q1 P p1 p2 → IsPullback (h ∘ k) m P p1 (q2 ∘ p2);  pullback_unpaste : IsPullback h m Q q1 q2 → k ∘ p1 ≈ q1 ∘ p2 → IsPullback (h ∘ k) m P p1 (q2 ∘ p2) → IsPullback k q1 P p1 p2.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. Both directions of the iff are proved, each with the right-hand square as hypothesis, exactly as stated. The extra hypothesis `Hcomm : k ∘ p1 ≈ q1 ∘ p2` in pullback_unpaste is not a weakening: the book supplies commutativity of BOTH squares as part of 'a commutative diagram', while the in-tree apex-pinned predicate cannot recover the left square's commutation from the outer rectangle alone (the file comment says so explicitly). The in-tree file header also records that an earlier draft transposed the two squares and that the proved statements are the standard pasting law.

evidence.intree_statement: Class Monic {x y} (f : x ~> y) := { monic : ∀ z (g1 g2 : z ~> x), f ∘ g1 ≈ f ∘ g2 → g1 ≈ g2 }.
Class Epic {x y} (f : x ~> y) := { epic : ∀ z (g1 g2 : y ~> z), g1 ∘ f ≈ g2 ∘ f → g1 ≈ g2 }.

statement_record.book: Definition 7.5: f : A → B is a monomorphism when the square with corners A, A, A, B whose two legs out of the apex are id_A and whose two legs into B are f is a PULLBACK; dually, f is an epimorphism when the corresponding square with corners A, B, B, B and legs f, f, id_B, id_B is a PUSHOUT. Informally, monos behave like injections and epis like surjections.
statement_record.intree: Class Monic {x y} (f : x ~> y) := { monic : ∀ z (g1 g2 : z ~> x), f ∘ g1 ≈ f ∘ g2 → g1 ≈ g2 }.  Class Epic {x y} (f : x ~> y) := { epic : ∀ z (g1 g2 : y ~> z), g1 ∘ f ≈ g2 ∘ f → g1 ≈ g2 }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on the presentation, same in extension. The two NOTIONS defined by the item are both in-tree, under the standard cancellation definition (and each is explicitly recorded as the other's C^op dual in the file comments, matching the book's dualization). What is NOT in-tree is the book's actual definiens: the equivalence 'Monic f ↔ IsPullback f f x id id' (and dually 'Epic f ↔ IsPushout f f y id id') is nowhere stated or proved, even though both IsPullback (Theory/Morphisms/Stability.v) and IsPushout (Structure/Pushout.v) exist and the proof is short. The closest in-tree relative, is_pullback_along_id : IsPullback id m y m id, is a DIFFERENT square (identity horizontals, m on both verticals — see ex7.7 part 2) that is a pullback for every m, monic or not.

gap: The pullback/pushout characterization that IS Definition 7.5 is absent. Searched `IsPullback f f`, `IsPullback ... id id`, `monic_iff`, `epic_iff`, `kernel_pair` + `Monic`: no lemma relates `Monic f` to the square being a pullback, and no lemma relates `Epic f` to the corresponding pushout. In-tree, `kernel_pair f` (Structure/Regular.v) is the pullback of f along itself but is never shown to be the diagonal exactly when f is monic. Only the cancellation definitions are available.

evidence.intree_statement: Lemma iso_pullback_stable {C : Category} {x y z : C} (f : x ~> z) (m : y ~> z) (Hm : IsIsomorphism m) (P : Pullback f m) : IsIsomorphism (pullback_fst f m P).
Lemma is_pullback_along_id {x y : C} (m : y ~> x) : IsPullback id m y m id.

statement_record.book: Exercise 7.7: (1) the pullback of an isomorphism i : B' → B along an arbitrary f : A → B is again an isomorphism (the induced i' : A' → A is iso); (2) for any map f : A → B the square whose two vertical legs are identities and whose two horizontal legs are f is a pullback.
statement_record.intree: (1) iso_pullback_stable : IsIsomorphism m → ∀ (P : Pullback f m), IsIsomorphism (pullback_fst f m P).  (2) is_pullback_along_id {x y} (m : y ~> x) : IsPullback id m y m id — the square with `id` on both horizontals and m on both verticals.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, both clauses. (1) matches literally: m is the iso being pulled back along an arbitrary f, and pullback_fst is the induced map opposite it; the inverse is built as the mediator of the cone (id, m⁻¹ ∘ f), exactly the intended proof. (2) is the book's square reflected across its diagonal (in-tree: identity HORIZONTALS with m on both verticals; book: identity VERTICALS with f on both horizontals) — the same square read with the two projections named in the other order, since IsPullback f g P p1 p2 and IsPullback g f P p2 p1 are interderivable by swapping the two conjuncts of the UMP. Both are stated for an arbitrary morphism, no extra hypotheses.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition Sets_Image_Factorization : Factorization f EpiClass MonoClass := @Build_Factorization Sets X Y f EpiClass MonoClass Sets_Image Sets_Image_epi Sets_Image_epi_epic Sets_Image_mono Sets_Image_mono_monic Sets_Image_comm.

Record Factorization {C : Category} {x y : C} (f : x ~> y) (E M : MorphismClass C) := { fact_mid : C; fact_e : x ~> fact_mid; fact_e_in : E _ _ fact_e; fact_m : fact_mid ~> y; fact_m_in : M _ _ fact_m; fact_comm : fact_m ∘ fact_e ≈ f }.
Theorem factorization_unique {O : OFS E M} {x y : C} {f : x ~> y} (F1 F2 : Factorization f E M) : ∃ i : fact_mid F1 ≅ fact_mid F2, (to i ∘ fact_e F1 ≈ fact_e F2) ∧ (fact_m F2 ∘ to i ≈ fact_m F1).

statement_record.book: Prose definition: f : C → D has an epi-mono factorization when there is an object im(f) with an epimorphism C ↠ im(f) and a monomorphism im(f) ↣ D composing to f. In Set every function factors as the surjection onto im(f) = {f(c) | c ∈ C} followed by the inclusion, and this factorization is unique up to isomorphism; the same holds in any topos — every f : c → d is e ; m with e epi and m mono.
statement_record.intree: Record Factorization f E M (the general (E,M)-factorization datum) instantiated at (EpiClass, MonoClass) by Sets_Image_Factorization for every f in Sets, with image object Sets_Image = { y : Y & { x : X & f x ≈ y } } compared by its Y-component; uniqueness up to iso is factorization_unique, which requires an `OFS E M` instance.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on two of the four clauses. The DEFINITION (clause a) is present as `Record Factorization` at (EpiClass, MonoClass), with the image object realized concretely. EXISTENCE IN SET (clause b) is fully present and axiom-free: Sets_Image_Factorization factors every morphism of Sets, the epi leg (Sets_Image_epi_epic) and mono leg (Sets_Image_mono_monic) both proved directly, needing no epis-are-surjections result. UNIQUENESS UP TO ISO (clause c) is only available through `factorization_unique`, which is stated over an `OFS E M` instance and hence needs orthogonality of E against M — and the library has NO `OFS EpiClass MonoClass` instance for Sets (only Abelian_OFS for abelian categories, Structure/Abelian.v:441, and Regular_OFS at (RegularEpi, Mono), Structure/Regular/Factorization.v:282, and there is no Regular instance for Sets). EXISTENCE IN A TOPOS (clause d) has no in-tree counterpart at all.

gap: Two clauses missing. (1) UNIQUENESS of the epi-mono factorization in Set: `factorization_unique` is conditioned on an `OFS E M` instance and the tree contains no `OFS EpiClass MonoClass` for Sets (nor a `Regular Sets` instance from which Regular_OFS could be drawn), so 'unique up to isomorphism' is unavailable for the very factorization Sets_Image_Factorization builds. evidence.intree_statement: Class Closed := { exponent_obj : obj → obj → obj where "y ^ x" := (exponent_obj x y); exp_iso {x y z} : x × y ~> z ≊ x ~> z^y; curry' := to exp_iso; uncurry' := from exp_iso; eval' {x y} : y^x × x ~> y := uncurry' id; ump_exponents' {x y z} (f : x × y ~> z) : eval' ∘ first (curry' f) ≈ f }.
Corollary curry_comp_l {x y z w : C} (f : y × z ~> w) (g : x ~> y) : curry f ∘ g ≈ curry (f ∘ first g).

Program Definition CCC_ClosedMonoidal : @ClosedMonoidal C := {| closed_is_cartesian := CC_CartesianMonoidal; exponent_obj := λ x y, @fobj _ _ (@InternalHomFunctor C _ CL) (x, y); exp_iso := @Cartesian.Closed.exp_iso C _ _ |}.

statement_record.book: Prose definition (with numbered display (7.10)): C is cartesian closed when its products give a symmetric monoidal structure with respect to which C is monoidal closed; concretely, for any objects C, D there is a hom-object D^C and an isomorphism C(A × C, D) ≅ C(A, D^C) natural in A — the currying bijection.
statement_record.intree: Class Closed := { exponent_obj : obj → obj → obj; exp_iso {x y z} : x × y ~> z ≊ x ~> z^y; ... ump_exponents' {x y z} (f : x × y ~> z) : eval' ∘ first (curry' f) ≈ f }.  Naturality in the first argument: curry_comp_l : curry f ∘ g ≈ curry (f ∘ first g).  The bridge to the book's monoidal phrasing: CCC_ClosedMonoidal : Closed → ClosedMonoidal over CC_CartesianMonoidal (the cartesian product read as a symmetric monoidal structure).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. `exp_iso : x × y ~> z ≊ x ~> z^y` is literally display (7.10) as an isomorphism of hom-setoids (the library's `≊` is the Sets-level iso of homsets), with the second product factor as the exponent — the same convention as the book's C(A × C, D) ≅ C(A, D^C). Naturality is not a class field but is derived: curry_comp_l gives naturality in A, and curry_comp / uncurry_comp / uncurry_comp_r give the remaining substitution laws. The book's second phrasing (products supply a symmetric monoidal structure with respect to which C is monoidal closed) is realized by CC_CartesianMonoidal + CCC_ClosedMonoidal, giving the CCC ⇒ cartesian-monoidal-closed direction. NOTE the same-name trap: `Structure/Closed.v` is an unrelated incomplete Eilenberg-Kelly stub; the live CCC development is Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v, which is what ElementaryTopos consumes.

evidence.intree_statement: Class ElementaryTopos (C : Category) := { topos_terminal : @Terminal C; topos_cartesian : @Cartesian C; topos_pullbacks : @HasPullbacks C; topos_closed : @Closed C topos_cartesian; topos_classifier : @SubobjectClassifier C topos_terminal }.

Definition FinSet_Topos : ElementaryTopos FinSet := {| topos_terminal := FinSet_Terminal; topos_cartesian := FinSet_Cartesian; topos_pullbacks := FinSet_Pullbacks; topos_closed := FinSet_Closed; topos_classifier := FinSet_Classifier |}.

Class SubobjectClassifier := { Ω : C; truth : 1 ~> Ω; char {u x : C} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) : x ~> Ω; char_pullback {u x} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) : IsPullback (char m M) truth u m one; char_unique {u x} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) (h : x ~> Ω) : IsPullback h truth u m one → h ≈ char m M }.

statement_record.book: Footnote 4: a category that has finite limits, is cartesian closed, and has a subobject classifier is called an elementary topos (contrasted with the Grothendieck notion; not developed further in the book).
statement_record.intree: Class ElementaryTopos (C : Category) := { topos_terminal : @Terminal C; topos_cartesian : @Cartesian C; topos_pullbacks : @HasPullbacks C; topos_closed : @Closed C topos_cartesian; topos_classifier : @SubobjectClassifier C topos_terminal }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, with one disclosed presentational caveat. The three clauses map one-to-one: finite limits ↦ topos_terminal + topos_cartesian + topos_pullbacks, cartesian closed ↦ topos_closed (the live Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v `Closed`, not the Structure/Closed.v stub), subobject classifier ↦ topos_classifier (Ω with monic truth, char, the classifying pullback square, and uniqueness). The caveat, stated in the file header, is that finite limits are carried EXPLICITLY as those three components rather than as a finite-completeness hypothesis, because the reduction of pullbacks to products and equalizers is not formalized in-tree; a terminal object together with pullbacks does generate every finite limit (Borceux I, 2.8.2), so the class is extensionally the book's definition, but no equalizer field and no derivation is provided. The definition is inhabited by a computable in-tree witness, FinSet_Topos (Pow 2 = 4 by eq_refl).
